videos.takeaway: Repeatable process (not luck): validate idea, build core loop fast, launch with ads, iterate on retention/playtime.

videos.takeaway: Devs quit from burnout and unrealistic expectations; ship many small games and treat failures as data.

videos.title: How I Made a Viral Roblox Game
videos.takeaway: Viral game case study: strong hook + polished thumbnails/icon/UI art; presentation quality drives click-through.

videos.takeaway: Comedic but accurate stages of Roblox dev (idea hype, scope creep, bugs, launch reality); plan for the unglamorous middle.

videos.takeaway: A viral game died because it lacked depth/updates; the sequel focused on longer-term progression and content cadence.

videos.title: Roblox Game Design Explained Like You're 5 Yrs Old
videos.takeaway: The '80/20 formula': ~80% proven mechanics players already understand, ~20% fresh twist/theme.

videos.title: Are YOU making these Game Dev Mistakes?
videos.takeaway: Common dev mistakes: no prototyping, polishing before fun is proven, building systems nobody uses, not playtesting with strangers.

videos.takeaway: Advertise correctly: test many thumbnails, small steady sponsor budgets, judge after several days, and fix the game before scaling spend.

videos.title: How to Boost your Game using Roblox Funnel Analytics
videos.takeaway: Use Roblox Funnel analytics: log each onboarding/core-loop step, find the biggest drop-off, fix that single step, repeat.

videos.title: The Secret To Making Your Roblox Game FUN! (Game Design)
videos.takeaway: Fun comes from clear goals + constant feedback + meaningful progress; test the core action in isolation before adding systems.

videos.title: How to Keep Players Engaged (Without Being Evil)
videos.takeaway: Ethical engagement: keep players through intrinsic motivation (mastery, curiosity, autonomy) instead of compulsion tricks; respect players' time and let them stop.

videos.title: How Game Designers Protect Players From Themselves
videos.takeaway: Players will optimize the fun out of a game; designers must shape incentives so the optimal strategy is also the fun one.

videos.title: What are retention metrics on Roblox?
videos.takeaway: Official explainer of D1/D7/D30 retention on the Creator Dashboard and why it's a key quality signal for recommendations.

videos.title: What are onboarding techniques on Roblox?
videos.takeaway: Official onboarding techniques: get to the fun quickly, teach by doing, use contextual hints, and give an early win.

videos.title: Onboarding Essentials
videos.takeaway: Roblox's onboarding essentials: fast early levels, starter items/currency, visible short/mid/long goals, a designed 'moment of joy', funnel each step.

videos.title: RDC 22: Creating an Intriguing First Time User Experience - Onett (Bee Swarm Simulator)
videos.takeaway: Bee Swarm Simulator's creator on FTUE: intrigue new players with an inviting world and immediate progress, then reveal depth gradually.

videos.title: How to Improve Your Roblox Game Stats FAST
videos.takeaway: Read your stats as a diagnosis: low playtime = weak loop, low D1 = weak FTUE/hook, low D7 = weak progression; fix the weakest first.

videos.title: How to Make a Great Mobile Game That Actually Keeps Players (and Makes Money)
videos.takeaway: Mobile retention: short sessions with clear goals, daily reasons to return, progression that's always visible.

videos.title: How To Get Back Into A Game, According to Science
videos.takeaway: Returning after a break is hard (forgotten controls/goals); 'welcome back' recaps and gentle re-onboarding reduce lapsed-player churn.

videos.title: How Path of Exile Keeps Players Coming Back | Path of Exile 2 & Grinding Gear Games
videos.takeaway: Path of Exile keeps players returning with regular content leagues (fresh starts), deep build mastery, and fair monetization.

videos.title: From Rational to Emotional: Designs that Increase Player Retention
videos.takeaway: GDC: move retention design from rational hooks (rewards) to emotional ones (attachment, identity, social belonging).

videos.title: It's About Time: System Design for Mobile Free-to-Play
videos.takeaway: GDC: time-based systems (timers, energy, daily cycles) structure F2P sessions; use them to create appointments, not walls.

videos.title: Getting Players to Care: Using Narrative to Drive Retention
videos.takeaway: GDC: narrative and character attachment give players emotional reasons to come back beyond rewards.

videos.title: I Studied 1,460 Onboarding Flows. Here's What I Found.
videos.takeaway: Study of 1,460 app onboarding flows: fewer steps, value shown before asks, progressive disclosure, personalization.

videos.title: Exploration in Games - Four Ways Players Discover Joy - Extra Credits
videos.takeaway: Four kinds of exploration (spatial, mechanical, narrative, social) each create curiosity; layered secrets reward continued play.

videos.title: Designing Addiction: The Twisted Psychology Of Game Design
videos.takeaway: Catalogue of compulsion techniques (variable rewards, loss aversion, sunk cost) - useful as a list of dark patterns to avoid or use carefully.

videos.title: Making Tutorials Feel Natural [Planning & Game Design]
videos.takeaway: Tutorials should feel like play: teach inside the real game with natural prompts, not walls of text.

videos.title: Being Kind to Beginners [Planning & Game Design]
videos.takeaway: Be kind to beginners: lower early difficulty, give generous early wins, let experts skip ahead.

videos.title: How To Grow A Small Roblox Game.
videos.takeaway: Small-game growth: tighten the first session, update often, and use stats (not gut feeling) to pick what to fix next.

videos.title: Roblox Changed the Algorithm.. Here’s How to Get Players Now
videos.takeaway: Recent algorithm changes weight long-term behavior (retention, returning players, friend invites) over launch-day spikes.

videos.title: How Gameplay Loops Keep You Playing
videos.channel: Adam Millard - The Architect of Games
videos.takeaway: Loops nest: moment-to-moment action, a session loop of goals, and a long-term loop of progression; each layer must be satisfying on its own.

videos.title: How To Design a Gameplay Loop
videos.takeaway: Design a loop as action → reward → upgrade → harder/better action, and make sure each step is clear to the player.

videos.title: Progression Systems - How Good Games Avoid Skinner Boxes - Extra Credits
videos.takeaway: Good progression unlocks new ways to play (variety, options), not just bigger numbers; pure stat treadmills feel like Skinner boxes.

videos.title: Core Game Loops
videos.takeaway: Timothy Cain (Fallout co-creator): define the core loop early, keep it simple, and test that the repeated action is enjoyable before content.

videos.title: What are loops in game design? - Loops - Game Design Theory
videos.takeaway: Explains loop terminology (core, meta, feedback loops) with examples; useful vocabulary for designing and documenting loops.

videos.title: How Video Game Economies are Designed
videos.takeaway: Game economies need balanced faucets (sources) and drains (sinks); unchecked inflation trivializes rewards.

videos.title: Leveling Up Progression Systems
videos.channel: Adam Millard - The Architect of Games
videos.takeaway: Progression systems should give players choices and expression; the anticipation of the next unlock is itself the reward.

videos.title: Gameplay Loops Are Out, Chains Are In
videos.takeaway: 'Chains' instead of loops: think of play as a sequence of goals that evolve and lead somewhere, not a circle that repeats unchanged.

videos.title: What Makes a Good Level Up System?
videos.takeaway: A good level-up system gives noticeable, felt power gains and meaningful choices at each level; invisible +1% upgrades don't motivate.

videos.title: The Real Core Loop - What Every Game Has In Common - Extra Credits
videos.takeaway: The real core loop every game shares: the player forms a goal, acts, gets feedback, and learns; design for that learning cycle.

videos.title: How Games Use Feedback Loops
videos.takeaway: Positive feedback loops snowball (winner gets stronger); negative loops (catch-up) keep things competitive; use them deliberately.

videos.title: Analytical Game Design: Core Loops, Compulsion Loops
videos.takeaway: Lecture contrasting healthy core loops with compulsion loops (reward-anticipation cycles); know which one you're building.

videos.title: Idle Games: The Mechanics and Monetization of Self-Playing Games
videos.takeaway: GDC: idle/incremental games run on exponential growth, prestige/reset loops and offline progress; monetize speed and automation.

videos.title: What makes an incremental game good?
videos.takeaway: Good incrementals keep introducing new mechanics/layers as numbers grow, so the game changes, not just the digits.

videos.title: 8 Cool Progression Based Mechanics in Games
videos.takeaway: Catalogue of creative progression mechanics (unlocks that change how you play) as alternatives to plain stat increases.

videos.title: 8 Cool Permanent Progression Mechanics in Games
videos.takeaway: Permanent (meta) progression mechanics that carry across runs/resets, keeping repeat play meaningful.

videos.title: How Great Games Do Progression | A Stardew Valley Video Essay
videos.takeaway: Stardew Valley: daily short-term goals feed seasonal/long-term goals; every session ends with progress made.

videos.title: Making a Tycoon in 2025 Pt.6 | Side Loops!

videos.title: Secrets of Game Feel and Juice
videos.takeaway: Game feel = responsive controls + layered feedback (animation, particles, sound, screen shake, hit-pause); tune it until actions feel good on their own.

videos.title: Juice it or lose it - a talk by Martin Jonasson & Petri Purho
videos.takeaway: 'Juice it or lose it': the same game transformed by tweening, squash/stretch, particles, sound and shake - juice multiplies satisfaction cheaply.

videos.title: Jan Willem Nijman - Vlambeer - "The art of screenshake" at INDIGO Classes 2013
videos.takeaway: Vlambeer's ~30 feel tricks: screen shake, hit-stop, big bullets/impacts, recoil/knockback, permanence (debris stays), sound punch.

videos.title: Can We Make This Button Fun To Press?
videos.takeaway: Even a single button press becomes fun with anticipation, squash, particles, sound and reaction - feedback design matters more than content.

videos.title: How to make your game 2X as fun! - (In No Time.)
videos.takeaway: Quick wins for fun: tighten feedback, add variety and surprise, reduce downtime and frustration.

videos.title: 10 Ways to Improve Game Feel
videos.takeaway: Ten concrete game-feel improvements: input buffering, coyote time, easing, camera work, impact frames, audio layering.

videos.title: The Two Types of Random in Game Design
videos.takeaway: Input randomness (before the player acts) creates interesting decisions; output randomness (after) can feel unfair - choose deliberately.

videos.title: This Psychological Trick Makes Rewards Backfire
videos.takeaway: Overjustification effect: heavy extrinsic rewards can make an intrinsically fun activity feel like a chore.

videos.title: How To Think Like A Game Designer
videos.takeaway: Think like a designer: start from the experience/feeling you want, then design mechanics that produce it.

videos.title: Risk and Reward  [Game Essence]
videos.takeaway: Sakurai: risk and reward should scale together; letting players choose bigger risk for bigger payoff creates tension and excitement.

videos.title: Stop for Big Moments! [Design Specifics]
videos.takeaway: Sakurai: briefly pause (hit-stop/slow-mo) on big moments so players register and savor them.

videos.title: Squeeze and Release [Game Essence]
videos.takeaway: Sakurai: alternate tension (squeeze) and release; relief after pressure is what makes peaks feel good.

videos.title: Pacing - How Games Keep Things Exciting - Extra Credits
videos.takeaway: Pacing: vary intensity like a wave - build-up, peak, rest - to avoid fatigue and boredom.

videos.title: Keeping players Interested - Pacing in Game Design
videos.takeaway: Keep players interested through pacing: introduce new mechanics/challenges regularly and give breathers between peaks.

videos.title: Non-Combat Gaming - How to Make Social Mechanics Fun - Extra Credits
videos.takeaway: Social mechanics are fun when players can cooperate, show off, and affect each other in meaningful but non-griefing ways.

videos.title: Intrinsic vs Extrinsic - Designing Good Rewards in Games - Extra Credits
videos.takeaway: Intrinsic rewards (mastery, curiosity, expression) outlast extrinsic ones; use extrinsic rewards to point at intrinsic fun.

videos.title: Sid Meier's Interesting Decisions
videos.takeaway: Sid Meier: a game is a series of interesting decisions - trade-offs with no single obvious answer, made with enough information.

videos.title: What Makes Games FUN (Psychology in Gaming)
videos.takeaway: Psychology of fun: competence, autonomy, relatedness (self-determination theory), plus flow from balanced challenge.

videos.title: WIRED by Design: A Game Designer Explains the Counterintuitive Secret to Fun
videos.takeaway: A designer's counterintuitive secret to fun: constraints and friction, used well, create challenge and meaning.
